title: Choose the MeetHalfway visual world
question: Pick the operating language for the complete redesign. All options retain the current fairness workflow and map behaviour.

options.label: Civic Route Ledger
options.lineage: public wayfinding desks and municipal transit service boards
options.thesis: A calm route-planning desk where every choice is legible, evidence-led, and shared.
options.viewport: The map holds the field while a structured decision rail turns locations, transport, and fairness into a visible route plan.
options.risk: Could feel too institutional if explanation and human names lose warmth.

raised.raise: The decision rail uses uncompromising tabular timing and clear state changes.
A single active route colour establishes hierarchy across the map and every selected state.

options.label: Shared Journey Studio
options.lineage: contemporary transport editorial and service-design workbooks
options.thesis: The group’s meeting plan unfolds as a clear story from origins to an agreed middle.
options.viewport: A generous map and concise step-by-step planning column make the fair result feel considered rather than calculated.
options.risk: Familiar for a polished mobility product, so the route evidence must carry the distinctive moment.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: travel documents and live departure boards
options.thesis: A shared journey is managed with the confidence of a live travel document.
options.viewport: Participant inputs become a single planning pass; recommendations re-rank as a live board beneath the map.
options.case: Strong timing clarity, but an individual travel-document metaphor is less natural for a group decision.
options.risk: Can overstate the formality of an informal meet-up.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Fairness becomes a visible interchange in a disciplined city-movement system.
options.viewport: A map-led workspace gives selected people and recommendations the authority of connected stations.
options.case: Excellent fit for routes and selection, but its dense transit language risks making the product feel specialist.
options.risk: Needs a restrained palette so the map remains easy to read.

options.label: Orienteering Map & Legend
options.thesis: A route course overlays terrain with active controls and a strict legend.
options.viewport: A purple course line leads across the map to a ranked legend of meeting decisions.
options.case: The map literacy is compelling, but the sporting frame does not identify with ordinary group coordination.
options.kept: A compact visual legend that makes every marker and recommendation immediately intelligible.
options.risk: Can prioritize the map metaphor over clarity for first-time users.

options.label: Metro Typographic Tiles
options.thesis: Large type and colour fields turn every status into a tile.
options.viewport: Panoramic tiles frame the planner as a series of bold status panels.
options.case: Strong visual authority, but the panorama competes with the map and hides the fairness comparison.
options.kept: One unmistakable accent colour for all live and selected states.
options.risk: Can become a visual identity exercise instead of a decision tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional, polished map app with a minimal sidebar.
canonCard.viewport: The expected app-shell arrangement, executed at a high craft level.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from a typical mapping product by design.
